newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: MOTORCYCLING-DOOHAN POWERS TO PROVISIONAL POLE.
newsitem.headline: MOTORCYCLING-DOOHAN POWERS TO PROVISIONAL POLE.

text.p: World champion Michael Doohan continued his domination of 500cc motorcycling on Friday by powering his Honda to provisional pole for Sunday's Austrian Grand Prix.
The Australian championship leader, who has won three of the season's four races so far, clocked one minute 29.654 seconds on his 24th of 27 practice laps.

His Honda team mate Tadayuki Okada was 0.147 seconds behind and the only other rider below the 1:30 barrier, despite still suffering from an injured left wrist sustained at the Italian race two weeks ago.
Both men went faster than their Spanish team mate Alex Criville's official lap record of 1:30.112 set during the 1996 Austrian race which was the first at the revised A1-Ring 4.318-km circuit.
Doohan, three-times world champion, was pleased with his performance but complained about grip problems and a slippery track.
"It's a complicated track although not really difficult to learn," he said. "You have to be careful with your lines. Off line there is even less grip than what you already have -- it's like ice."
Last year's winner here, Criville, visited the gravel traps twice during the hour-long session and posted only the seventh time.
"I out-braked myself twice. I can't feel the track through the bike here, especially through the front wheel," he said.
Criville trails Doohan in the standings by 17 points.
Spain's Carlos Checa, also on a Honda, posted the third best time of 1:30.258 while Italian Yamaha rider Luca Cadalora, the only non-Honda racer in the top eight, was fourth fastest in 1:30.785.
"I'm happy to have found a good setting at this track so quickly," said Cadalora, also the first non-Honda rider to make the podium this season with a second place in Mugello.
The final qualifying session is on Saturday.
